title: Building an idle dungeon crawler - What's been helpful and not.
author: cephaswilco
selftext:
I've been making games professionally for nearly 10 years now, I'm just gonna share what's been helpful for AI and where I've had some dead ends. This will likely be my first actual personal/solo release.   
  
I'm making Kinfall, an idle dungeon crawler where a family of heroes fights and loots on its own, you can play it traditionally or turn on Auto Mode and have it docked to the right or bottom and play itself. 

The game was inspired by my brother botting Diablo 2 years ago and realizing it would be fun to have a legit game that just botted. 

For Kinfall and ARPGs you need a lot of procedural levels, gear and stats balancing.  
AI has been great for this.  
  
In terms of balance alone, it's incredibly helpful to just write a small applet/tool that can show stats on the fly and compare to other items/builds/enemies etc.   
  
The greatest strength I've found is being able to build any helpful tool that I might not have felt necessary in the past, but now that I can build the tool quickly and validate it's usefulness immediately, I just build a lot more small tools. 

In terms of Art, AI has been very useful for me to get the vision of the game off the ground. I have been slowly moving over to less AI gen art for the project because it's still very hard to advertise/promote with the gen AI. So for pragmatic reasons, I've been making the swap where it makes most sense. 

Coming to Steam, demo on the way: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5470880/Kinfall\_An\_Idle\_Dungeon\_Crawler/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=organic&utm\_campaign=post\_v2&utm\_content=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5470880/Kinfall_An_Idle_Dungeon_Crawler/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=post_v2&utm_content=aigamedev)

  
I've always wanted to build this game but life/other side projects/responsibility got in the way.   
It was always a bit of a passion project, but it's nice to validate by attempting to sell it.  
Anyways, I've been using AI for programming for 1.5 years now, but something changed with Claude Opus 5.5 where I could essentially build very deep systems, and validate them, quickly, so I thought that this old project was the perfect template.

I've seen quite a few other ARPG/Diablo adjacent auto clickers on this sub, so a lot of us must be on a similar wavelength.  
  
I think I'm getting good at this (AI game dev), it helps that I've been a programmer, lead, and project manager across my career. 

If you have any questions of specifics, I'm happy to share.
